metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Some cited company-adoption lists come from KMP-focused marketing/consultancy blogs (2026 SEO content) rather than primary company engineering blogs; these were corroborated across multiple independent sources but not verified against original company sources directly. JetBrains-sourced statistics (survey and telemetry) are vendor-provided, though the IntelliJ telemetry study is presented as measured usage data rather than self-reported preference.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--kotlin): Kotlin has a full, mature third-party tool stack spanning every predeclared category (IDE, linter, formatter, static analysis, build systems, CI/CD, frameworks, package repositories, testing), largely because it sits on the JVM/Android tooling ecosystem while also adding Kotlin-native tools (ktlint, detekt, Ktor, KSP). Coverage is broad and depth in each category is strong (multiple competing/complementary tools such as ktlint+detekt+Spotless+Android Lint), though slightly narrower than Java's absolute tool count in some enterprise-legacy niches (e.g. very old APM/profiler integrations built Java-first). Normalized score: 94/100.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Evidence drawn from blog posts, vendor documentation, and GitHub project pages rather than a single authoritative registry; some sources are SEO-style 2026 roundup articles whose company/tool lists could not be independently cross-verified beyond the citations shown.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.
